name: intake-validation-normalization
prompt: Review how incoming lead records are classified and normalized against the normative specs. Read /app/src/spec/lead_schema.json and /app/src/spec/lead_policy.json first, then trace how a lead record (a single object or an array) moves through src/lib/validation.ts, src/lib/payload.ts, and src/lib/spec.ts. Check how each field is normalized (whitespace, casing, phone and email formats, state and service values), which fields are required for the accepted, incomplete, and invalid outcomes, how the legacy-schema and Facebook webhook shapes are mapped onto canonical fields, and how a batch array is validated as a unit under the batchSubmission contract. Compare each rule, default, and mapping in the code against the spec text. Report every place where the code accepts, rejects, or classifies a lead differently from the specs, or where a field is dropped or altered incorrectly during normalization. Do not modify any files.

name: ledger-reconciliation-outputs
prompt: Review the persistence and reconciliation layer against the normative specs. Read /app/src/spec/lead_schema.json first, focusing on the matchedSubmission, promotion, sourceGrouping, and rejected-ledger contracts, then read src/lib/ledger.ts and src/lib/outputs.ts. Check how existing crm_leads.json and incomplete_leads.json records are loaded and whether accepted records can ever be mutated. Check how a submission whose identity matches an existing record is compared against the recorded canonical fields. Check whether incomplete-to-complete promotion preserves the original first-contact timestamp. Check how lead_sources.json is derived from the ledgers and whether its grouping and counts match the sourceGrouping contract. Check how malformed ledgers are detected and recorded in rejected_ledgers.json. Check how output files are written, including whether a failure on any target path could leave some ledgers already changed or leave a stale submission.json in place. Report every point where the behavior diverges from these contracts. Do not modify any files.

name: entrypoint-calendar-ui-wiring
prompt: Review timestamping, the shared entry point, and the form behavior against the specs and the stated requirements. Read /app/src/spec/business_calendar.json and src/lib/calendar.ts, and check how output timestamps are computed deterministically from the calendar rules, including timezone, business-day, and cutoff handling. Then read src/lib/submitLead.ts, src/scripts/submit.ts, src/lib/tracking.ts, src/App.tsx, src/components/LeadForm.tsx, and src/main.tsx. Confirm that the exported submitLead function matches the API in lead_schema.json, that the React form and the npm submit script both call that same function and do not write artifacts directly, and that the field labels, placeholders, and Consent checkbox label match the required text exactly. Check that the success state appears only when the pipeline result is accepted, and that after a rejected submission the form stays visible and keeps the values the user typed. Report every divergence from these requirements. Do not modify any files.
